A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forecasting study. All 12 pages of v3 and 10 pages of v4 support comparison, including equations, three figures, one table, and references. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V3 reports original model-training experiments, accuracy and calibration measurements on 1,265 forecasting questions, failure analyses, and simulated Polymarket trading results.

after.justification: V4 retains the original forecasting experiments, calibration measurements, failure analyses, and trading simulations.

M1.justification: The base model, reward design, GRPO/Modified-GRPO/ReMax procedures, guardrails, chronological training, and prediction ensemble remain unchanged. The added Foresight Learning explanation documents existing data generation rather than establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Polymarket questions, generated forecasting questions, and the same test set of 1,265 questions. V4's additional example questions illustrate existing coverage rather than introducing new tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figure 1, Table 1, and Figure 2. DPO, untuned DeepSeek-R1 14B, OpenAI o1, and market prices remain in their respective comparisons; the trading figure retains both single-model and ensemble ReMax results.

E3.justification: The conclusion corrects the stated training total from 100k questions (10k real plus 90k synthetic) to 110k (10k Polymarket plus 100k generated). This agrees with Section 2.1 already in v3 and is a reported-setting correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Test and trading protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 2.5 retains the same overconfidence and gibberish examples and frequencies. The algorithm comparisons and market-confidence analysis in Figures 1 and 3 are also unchanged; no new ablation, robustness test, or case analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both retain paired comparisons, 95% Wald intervals for Brier scores, bootstrap intervals for ECE, and two-sided significance tests. No new seed information, repeated-training-run counts, or uncertainty reporting practices are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1's values and significance markers are unchanged, including ReMax Ensemble-7's Brier score of 0.190 and ECE of 0.062. All three figure images are identical. Reported trading profits and findings by market confidence also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The reward, advantage, and optimization equations retain the same mathematical content. The bounded-Brier explanation is retained in a relocated footnote. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: Both claim that a compact RL-trained forecaster can match or surpass frontier-model accuracy, improve calibration, and produce profitable hypothetical Polymarket trades. Revised introductory wording aligns with claims already present in v3's abstract and results rather than expanding the contribution.

C2.justification: V4 adds a specific warning against interpreting prediction-market simulations as estimates of financial-trading impact, discusses computational accessibility, and introduces broader-impact discussion of decision risks, reasoning-trace interpretability, and human oversight. Existing interpretations of the experimental findings remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a test-dataset link and describes its questions, headlines, reasoning traces, predictions, and outcomes. It also explains Foresight Learning at a high level and reports approximately three days on eight H100 GPUs. These are additional disclosures; existing hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to RLVR, Dr. GRPO, and earlier forecasting research remain unchanged. The altered Lambert et al. reference title is bibliographic rather than a change in cited research.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized proofreading edits, expands explanations of synthetic-data generation and prediction-market shares, adds publication/contact information, and introduces a Broader Impact section. The existing section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The journal formatting adds a running publication header, changes margins, and reflows the retained figures and table. Figure 1 now precedes Results, while Figure 3 appears within the Broader Impact pagination. Plot content, captions, and table organization remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 improves transparency through dataset-access information, a generation overview, and runtime disclosure. It also reconciles the conclusion's training count with the methods and more carefully bounds the interpretation of trading profits. These are useful, limited improvements; the underlying methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
